URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx2vd3qgjy9o
NOTE: BBC (21 Jul) — June govt borrowing £16bn, ~£7.9bn lower than a year earlier. Ruth Gregory (deputy chief UK economist, Capital Economics): June figure "a rare piece of good news" for Burnham and Healey, but "there's no escaping the fact that the public finances are fragile and that there is limited scope for extra borrowing." James Smith (chief UK economist, ING): borrowing still ahead of OBR projections "a reminder of the challenges that the new chancellor and the new prime minister face." Healey (Mon statement): "fiscal credibility is the bedrock for economic stability and for national security." Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride: "If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control." Darren Jones (sacked) accused govt of an unfunded tax cut.
